+# Pull-request staging environment for a RAILS app (FRAMEWORK=rails).
+# Copied into the app repo as .github/workflows/staging.yml by the bootstrap.
+#
+# Opening a PR against main stands a complete second copy of the app up on the
+# SAME droplet, serving on <app>-stg.<zone>; closing the PR destroys it. Pushing
+# to an open PR redeploys it. Jobs: test (gate) -> build+push -> deploy, and a
+# separate destroy job on `closed`.
+#
+# The Rails path is SQLite-only, so this workflow has no Postgres branch. The
+# environment's isolation from production comes from three things:
+#
+#   * its own compose project (<slug>-stg) — its own containers and its own
+#     app_data volume, so its database is a different file on a different volume
+#   * litestream.staging.yml, which replicates into that volume instead of Spaces
+#   * compose.override.yaml, which switches off the archive-to-Spaces loop
+#
+# Between them the environment holds no Spaces credentials at all, and cannot
+# write into the prefixes production restores from.
+#
+# ONE ENVIRONMENT PER APP, not one per PR: there is a single staging name, so
+# there is a single slot. The most recent PR to deploy holds it, recorded in
+# .staging-owner on the droplet. A second PR takes the slot over — destroying the
+# first PR's environment as it does — and closing a PR only tears the
+# environment down if that PR still owns it.
+#
+# Required repo config (seeded by bootstrap):
+#   var    STAGING_DOMAIN             - <app>-stg.<zone>; ABSENT DISABLES THIS
+#                                       WORKFLOW ENTIRELY (every job is gated on
+#                                       it), which is how an app whose infra/
+#                                       predates staging stays untouched
+#   plus the same DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN / SSH_PRIVATE_KEY / DOCR_REGISTRY /
+#   FIREWALL_ID / DROPLET_HOST / APP_SLUG the production deploy uses
+#
+# There is NO staging secret to maintain: the environment's signing key is
+# derived from SECRET_KEY_BASE inside the deploy job (one-way, fixed label), so
+# it differs from production's without anyone setting a second secret per app or
+# per pull request.
+name: staging
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, closed]
+
+# One staging operation at a time for the whole repo — deploys and teardowns
+# alike. The slot is a single directory on a single droplet, so two PRs racing
+# to claim it must be serialized rather than merged. Queue rather than cancel:
+# an interrupted teardown leaks an environment, and an interrupted deploy can
+# leave migrations half-applied.
+concurrency:
+  group: staging-${{ github.repository }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  # The deploy comments the environment's URL on the PR.
+  pull-requests: write
+
+env:
+  REGISTRY: registry.digitalocean.com
+  # The PR number is the staging slot's owner, and part of every staging image
+  # tag — the teardown finds both by it.
+  PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
+
+jobs:
+  # Red tests block the staging deploy exactly as they block production's.
+  test:
+    # Three gates, all of them load-bearing:
+    #   * `closed` runs the destroy job instead
+    #   * no STAGING_DOMAIN means this app has no staging environment wired
+    #   * a PR from a FORK gets no secrets from GitHub, and must not: this
+    #     workflow holds the droplet's SSH key and the DO API token, and would
+    #     hand both to code nobody has reviewed. Such PRs are skipped, not failed.
+    if: >-
+      github.event.action != 'closed'
+      && vars.STAGING_DOMAIN != ''
+      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    env:
+      RAILS_ENV: test
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      # `ruby-version: .ruby-version`, not `ruby-version-file:` — see the note in
+      # deploy.ruby.yml: the file input is rejected by older resolutions of @v1.
+      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
+        with:
+          ruby-version: .ruby-version
+          bundler-cache: true
+
+      # Prepare the isolated test database before the Rails suite gates deployment.
+      - name: Run tests
+        run: |
+          bundle exec rails db:prepare
+          bundle exec rails test
+
+  build:
+    needs: test
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest # native amd64
+    outputs:
+      app_name: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.app_name }}
+      image: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}
+      tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

+          if [ -z "$app_name" ]; then echo "::error::.app-name is empty or missing"; exit 1; fi
+          echo "app_name=$app_name" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "image=${REGISTRY}/${{ vars.DOCR_REGISTRY }}/${app_name}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          # Staging images share the app's registry repository (the free tier
+          # allows exactly one) and are told apart by tag. The tag names the PR
+          # AND pins the commit: the PR part is what the teardown deletes, the
+          # SHA part is what keeps the deploy immutable. It is the PR's HEAD sha
+          # rather than github.sha, which for a pull_request event is the
+          # ephemeral merge commit and means nothing once the PR closes.
+          echo "tag=pr-${PR}-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

+      - name: Install doctl
+        uses: digitalocean/action-doctl@v2
+        with:
+          token: ${{ secrets.DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Log in to DO Container Registry
+        run: doctl registry login --expiry-seconds 1200
+
+      - name: Set up Buildx
+        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
+
+      # No :latest here — that tag is production's, and a staging build must
+      # never become what an unpinned pull resolves to.
+      - name: Build and push image
+        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7

+# Runtime stack on the droplet for a RAILS app (FRAMEWORK=rails, which
+# always implies the SQLite backend). Copied to the app repo as
+# deploy/compose.yaml by the bootstrap. It mirrors compose.sqlite.yaml (the
+# Phoenix+SQLite stack) — same Litestream sidecar + restore, same blue/green
+# swap, same shared-Caddy routing — but boots a Rack/Puma app instead of an OTP
+# release:
+#
+#   * The app service runs `puma` (image CMD), not `bin/<app> start`. There is
+#     no PHX_SERVER gate and no APP_NAME — a Rack app serves unconditionally on
+#     $PORT.
+#   * Migrations run `rails db:prepare` (Active Record) in the one-off migrate
+#     runner, not `bin/<app> eval '<Module>.Release.migrate()'`.
+#   * The DB is a SQLite file on a NAMED DOCKER VOLUME (app_data -> /data),
+#     shared by both colors + the migrate runner. Litestream streams its WAL to
+#     Spaces continuously and restores it on a recreated droplet.
+#
+# Interpolated values (${...}) come from .env, written over SSH at deploy time:
+#   IMAGE            full image ref incl tag, e.g. registry.../app:<sha> (SHA-pinned)
+#   DOMAIN           public FQDN (matches the DNSimple A record / cert)
+#   APP_SLUG         this app's slug — names the compose project + network aliases
+#   DATABASE_PATH    on-volume path to the SQLite file, e.g. /data/app.db
+#   SECRET_KEY_BASE  Rack session secret (Rails `set :sessions`)
+#   LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID / LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY   Spaces keypair
+#   BACKUP_BUCKET / BACKUP_ENDPOINT / BACKUP_REGION / BACKUP_PATH   replica target
+#
+# No secrets live in this file — only references. (locked decision 12)
+#
+# There is no proxy here: TLS and routing belong to the droplet's SHARED Caddy
+# (deploy/edge-compose.yaml, installed at /root/caddy), because one droplet can
+# host several apps and only one process can own :443. This stack joins the
+# shared `edge` network and publishes per-color aliases Caddy dials by name.
+
+# Every app on the droplet gets its own compose project, so its containers and
+# volumes (<slug>_app_data) can't collide with a neighbour's.
+name: ${APP_SLUG}
+
+# Shared definition for both colors (and the one-off migrate runner).
+x-app: &app
+  image: ${IMAGE}
+  restart: unless-stopped
+  env_file:
+    - .env
+  environment:
+    RAILS_ENV: "production"
+    RACK_ENV: "production"
+    # URL host for generated links; Rails reads APP_HOST where it builds URLs.
+    APP_HOST: ${DOMAIN}
+    PORT: "4000"
+    # SQLite file path (config/database.rb reads DATABASE_PATH).
+    DATABASE_PATH: ${DATABASE_PATH}
+  volumes:
+    # The SQLite file lives here, shared with the migrate runner + Litestream.
+    - app_data:/data
+  depends_on:
+    # Restore + permission fix must finish before the app opens the DB...
+    db_init:
+      condition: service_completed_successfully
+    # ...and the replicator must be running so writes are streamed off-box.
+    litestream:
+      condition: service_started
+  expose:
+    # Internal only — never published to the host. Caddy reaches it by name.
+    - "4000"
+  networks:
+    - web
+  healthcheck:
+    # Alive = the endpoint answers HTTP at all (HTTP 200 from /health).
+    # bash + /dev/tcp because the slim runtime image has no curl/wget.
+    test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/4000 && printf 'GET /health HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n' >&3 && grep -q '^HTTP/1.[01] 200 ' <&3"]
+    interval: 5s
+    timeout: 3s
+    retries: 12
+    start_period: 10s
+
+# Shared Litestream config: both the restore and replicate services read the
+# same /etc/litestream.yml (env-expanded against .env).
+x-litestream: &litestream
+  image: litestream/litestream:0.3.14
+  env_file:
+    - .env
+  volumes:
+    - app_data:/data
+    - ./litestream.yml:/etc/litestream.yml:ro
+  networks:
+    - web
+
+services:
+  # One-shot, runs as root before anything opens the DB. Two jobs:
+  #   1. Restore the SQLite file from Spaces IFF /data has no DB yet and a replica
+  #      exists (first-ever deploy: both false -> no-op; recreated droplet: empty
+  #      volume + existing replica -> full restore).
+  #   2. chown /data to the app's runtime uid (Debian 'nobody' = 65534) so the
+  #      app, which runs unprivileged, can create the DB + its -wal/-shm files.
+  # $$DATABASE_PATH is escaped so the container shell (not compose) expands it.
+  db_init:
+    <<: *litestream
+    restart: "no"
+    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
+    command:
+      - litestream restore -if-db-not-exists -if-replica-exists "$$DATABASE_PATH" && chown -R 65534:65534 /data
+
+  # Long-running: continuously replicate the WAL to Spaces. Runs as root (it can
+  # still read the nobody-owned DB and write its own shadow files under /data).
+  litestream:
+    <<: *litestream
+    restart: unless-stopped
+    command: ["replicate"]
+    depends_on:
+      db_init:
+        condition: service_completed_successfully
+
+  # The two colors are the only services on the shared `edge` network, and each
+  # carries a slug-qualified alias there — that name is what the droplet's Caddy
+  # dials (see deploy/site.caddy.tmpl). The alias must be unique ACROSS apps:
+  # every app on the host shares this network, so a bare `app_blue` would be
+  # ambiguous and Caddy would round-robin into someone else's app.
+  #
+  # `networks` is re-declared rather than inherited because the alias differs per
+  # color; a YAML merge key can't vary a value between the two.
+  app_blue:
+    <<: *app
+    networks:
+      web: {}
+      edge:
+        aliases:
+          - ${APP_SLUG}-blue
+
+  app_green:
+    <<: *app
+    networks:
+      web: {}
+      edge:
+        aliases:
+          - ${APP_SLUG}-green
+
+  # One-off migration runner (profile keeps it out of `up -d`):
+  #   docker compose run --rm migrate bundle exec rails db:prepare
+  # Never serves traffic, so it stays off `edge`.
+  migrate:
+    <<: *app
+    restart: "no"
+    profiles: ["tools"]
+
+volumes:
+  app_data:
+
+networks:
+  # Private to this app: the sidecars talk to nothing outside the project.
+  web:
+  # The droplet-wide network the shared Caddy is on. Created by edge.sh, external
+  # because it outlives any single app — tearing this stack down must not
+  # disconnect the other apps on the host.
+  edge:
+    external: true

+# supported backend for the Rails path — the runtime carries libsqlite3 and
+# the DB file lives on a droplet volume (Litestream replicates it; see

+# file; RUBY_VERSION is an explicit override.

+

+  && apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

+# without the target Ruby), so bundler resolves from the Gemfile here and the
+# resulting image is the immutable, SHA-pinned artifact.

+    BUNDLE_WITHOUT="development:test" \

+# React static deployment: test and typecheck/build before uploading any release.
+name: deploy
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  # Redeploy whatever is on main without pushing a commit. Repo variables
+  # (DOMAIN, APP_SLUG, DROPLET_HOST) are not reflected in git, so changing one
+  # otherwise has no way to reach the droplet: a bootstrap re-run that finds
+  # nothing to commit triggers no deploy, and the old value keeps serving.
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# One deploy at a time; queue rather than cancel so a publish is never
+# interrupted half-way.
+concurrency:
+  group: deploy-${{ gitea.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  deploy:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    env:
+      HOST: ${{ vars.DROPLET_HOST }}
+      APP_SLUG: ${{ vars.APP_SLUG }}
+      STACK_DIR: /root/apps/${{ vars.APP_SLUG }}
+      RELEASE: ${{ gitea.sha }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version-file: .node-version
+          cache: npm
+      - name: Install locked dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+      - name: Test application
+        run: npm test
+      - name: Build static application
+        run: |
+          rm -rf dist
+          npm run build
+          test -s dist/index.html || { echo "::error::build produced no dist/index.html"; exit 1; }
+
+      # Ship one file, not a directory tree: a tarball is a single scp and it
+      # extracts atomically enough that a half-uploaded release can't be
+      # published (publish.sh runs only after extraction succeeds).
+      - name: Package release
+        run: tar -czf site.tgz -C dist .
+
+      # No firewall hole-punch here (see file header) — the runner's IP is
+      # already allow-listed for SSH, statically, in infra-app/firewall.tf.
+      - name: Configure SSH
+        env:
+          SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SSH_PRIVATE_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          bash deploy/ci/configure-ssh.sh
+
+      - name: Create stack directories
+        run: |
+          ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new root@"$HOST" \
+            "mkdir -p /root/caddy/sites '$STACK_DIR/releases/$RELEASE'"
+
+      # /root/caddy is the SHARED edge proxy — one per droplet, host-owned. Every

+

+# React static deployment: test and typecheck/build before uploading any release.
+name: deploy
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  # Redeploy whatever is on main without pushing a commit. Repo variables
+  # (DOMAIN, APP_SLUG, DROPLET_HOST) are not reflected in git, so changing one
+  # otherwise has no way to reach the droplet: a bootstrap re-run that finds
+  # nothing to commit triggers no deploy, and the old value keeps serving.
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# One deploy at a time; queue rather than cancel so a publish is never
+# interrupted half-way.
+concurrency:
+  group: deploy-${{ gitea.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  deploy:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    env:
+      HOST: ${{ vars.DROPLET_HOST }}
+      APP_SLUG: ${{ vars.APP_SLUG }}
+      STACK_DIR: /root/apps/${{ vars.APP_SLUG }}
+      RELEASE: ${{ gitea.sha }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version-file: .node-version
+          cache: npm
+      - name: Install locked dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+      - name: Test application
+        run: npm test
+      - name: Build static application
+        run: |
+          rm -rf dist
+          npm run build
+          test -s dist/index.html || { echo "::error::build produced no dist/index.html"; exit 1; }
+
+      # Ship one file, not a directory tree: a tarball is a single scp and it
+      # extracts atomically enough that a half-uploaded release can't be
+      # published (publish.sh runs only after extraction succeeds).
+      - name: Package release
+        run: tar -czf site.tgz -C dist .
+
+      # No firewall hole-punch here (see file header) — the runner's IP is
+      # already allow-listed for SSH, statically, in infra-app/firewall.tf.
+      - name: Configure SSH
+        env:

+APP_DIR="${1:-}"
+[ -n "$APP_DIR" ] || fail 'usage: new-react-app.sh <app_dir>'
+name="$(basename "$APP_DIR")"
+case "$name" in
+  ''|*[!a-z0-9_-]*|[!a-z]*) fail 'app directory name must start with a lowercase letter and contain lowercase letters, digits, underscores or hyphens' ;;

+if [ -f "$APP_DIR/package.json" ]; then
+  python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/validate-react-app.py" "$APP_DIR"

+  if [ -d "$APP_DIR" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$APP_DIR")" ]; then
+    fail 'directory is not empty; refusing to scaffold over existing files'

+  mkdir -p "$APP_DIR"
+  cp -R "$ROOT/app-react/." "$APP_DIR/"
+  cp "$ROOT/test/fixtures/react/App.test.tsx" "$APP_DIR/src/App.test.tsx"
+  python3 - "$APP_DIR" "$name" <<'PY'
+import json

+    data = json.loads((root / file).read_text())
+    data['name'] = sys.argv[2]
+    if file == 'package-lock.json':
+        data['packages']['']['name'] = sys.argv[2]
+    (root / file).write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + '\n')

+# migrate, THEN load the models + app (config/environment).

+  config.include RequestHelpers, type: :request
+  config.include RequestHelpers, type: :feature
+
+  # Each example runs in a transaction rolled back at the end — fast, isolated,
+  # and safe against SQLite's single writer (one connection throughout).
+  config.around(:each) do |example|
+    DB.transaction(rollback: :always, savepoint: true) { example.run }
+  end
+
+  config.order = :random
+  config.expect_with(:rspec) { |c| c.syntax = :expect }
+end

+#!/usr/bin/env ruby
+# Offline scaffold and CI command-boundary contracts for mandatory acceptance tests.
+require 'fileutils'
+require 'open3'
+require 'tmpdir'
+require 'yaml'
+ROOT = File.expand_path('..', __dir__)
+FIXTURES = File.join(ROOT, 'test/fixtures/acceptance')
+
+def run!(*command, **options)
+  output, status = Open3.capture2e(*command, **options)
+  abort "#{command.inspect}: #{output}" unless status.success?
+  output
+end
+
+def assert(condition, message)
+  abort message unless condition
+end
+
+Dir.mktmpdir('acceptance-scaffolds') do |work|
+  %w[sinatra mix escript phoenix].each do |kind|
+    app = File.join(work, kind, 'acceptance_app')
+    FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(app))
+    environment = {'APP_EXTRA_DEPS' => '', 'CD_NO_SETUP' => '1'}
+    if kind == 'phoenix'
+      FileUtils.mkdir_p(app)
+      File.write(File.join(app, 'mix.exs'), <<~ELIXIR)

+          def project do
+            [app: :acceptance_app, version: "0.1.0", elixir: "~> 1.15", deps: deps()]
+          end
+          defp deps do
+            [{:phoenix, "~> 1.8"}]
+          end
+        end
+      ELIXIR
+      File.write(File.join(app, '.formatter.exs'), '[inputs: ["{mix,.formatter}.exs", "{config,lib,test}/**/*.{ex,exs}"]]')
+      run!(environment, 'bash', File.join(ROOT, 'scripts/setup-cucumberex.sh'), app, kind)
+      assert(File.read(File.join(ROOT, 'scripts/bootstrap/app.sh')).include?('setup-cucumberex.sh'), 'fresh Phoenix bootstrap omits mandatory acceptance setup')
+    else
+      command = kind == 'sinatra' ? ['scripts/new-sinatra-app.sh'] : ['scripts/new-mix-app.sh', kind == 'mix' ? '--lib' : '--escript']
+      command[0] = File.join(ROOT, command[0])
+      run!(environment, 'bash', *command, app)
+    end
+    Dir.glob(File.join(FIXTURES, kind, '**', '*')).select { |path| File.file?(path) }.each do |fixture|
+      relative = fixture.sub(File.join(FIXTURES, kind) + '/', '')
+      expected = File.read(fixture).gsub('__APP_MODULE__', 'AcceptanceApp')
+      actual = File.join(app, relative)
+      assert(File.file?(actual), "#{kind}: omitted #{relative}")
+      assert(File.read(actual) == expected, "#{kind}: #{relative} differs from accepted behavior fixture")

  output
end

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Install acceptance tooling only into a freshly generated Elixir project.
+# This is independent of optional documentation and APP_EXTRA_DEPS.
+set -euo pipefail
+APP_DIR="${1:?usage: setup-cucumberex.sh APP_DIR phoenix|mix|escript}"
+KIND="${2:?missing project kind}"
+case "$KIND" in phoenix|mix|escript) ;; *) echo "unsupported project kind: $KIND" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+. "$SCRIPT_DIR/app-meta.sh"
+APP_MODULE="$(app_module "$APP_DIR")"
+python3 - "$APP_DIR" <<'PYTHON'
+import pathlib
+import re
+import sys
+
+root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
+mixfile = root / "mix.exs"
+text = mixfile.read_text()
+if not re.search(r"\{:cucumberex,", text):
+    text, count = re.subn(r"(defp deps do\s*\[)", r'\1\n      {:cucumberex, "~> 0.2.1", only: [:dev, :test], runtime: false},', text, count=1)
+    if count != 1:
+        raise SystemExit("Cannot find fresh project's deps list")
+if not re.search(r"cucumber:\s*:test", text):
+    if "preferred_envs:" in text:
+        text, count = re.subn(r"preferred_envs:\s*\[", "preferred_envs: [cucumber: :test, ", text, count=1)
+    elif re.search(r"def cli do\s*\[", text):
+        text, count = re.subn(r"(def cli do\s*\[)", r"\1preferred_envs: [cucumber: :test], ", text, count=1)
+    else:
+        text, count = re.subn(r"  defp deps do", "  def cli do\n    [preferred_envs: [cucumber: :test]]\n  end\n\n  defp deps do", text, count=1)
+    if count != 1:
+        raise SystemExit("Cannot configure fresh project's cucumber test environment")
+mixfile.write_text(text)
+formatter = root / ".formatter.exs"
+text = formatter.read_text()
+if "features/**/*.{ex,exs}" not in text:
+    text, count = re.subn(r"inputs:\s*\[", 'inputs: ["features/**/*.{ex,exs}", ', text, count=1)
+    if count != 1:
+        raise SystemExit("Cannot find fresh project's formatter inputs")
+if ":cucumberex" not in text:
+    if "import_deps:" in text:
+        text, count = re.subn(r"import_deps:\s*\[", "import_deps: [:cucumberex, ", text, count=1)
+    else:
+        text, count = re.subn(r"\[", "[\n  import_deps: [:cucumberex],", text, count=1)
+    if count != 1:
+        raise SystemExit("Cannot configure fresh project's formatter imports")
+formatter.write_text(text)
+PYTHON
+mkdir -p "$APP_DIR/bin" "$APP_DIR/features/support" "$APP_DIR/features/step_definitions"
+cat > "$APP_DIR/bin/check-features" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+export MIX_ENV=test
+exec mix cucumber --format pretty --strict
+ACCEPTANCE
+chmod +x "$APP_DIR/bin/check-features"
+case "$KIND" in
+  phoenix)
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/home.feature" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+Feature: Application home page
+  Scenario: Render the application home page
+    When I visit the application home page
+    Then the application renders its welcome page
+ACCEPTANCE
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/step_definitions/home_steps.ex" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+defmodule __APP_MODULE__.HomeSteps do
+  use Cucumberex.DSL
+  import ExUnit.Assertions
+  import Phoenix.ConnTest
+
+  @endpoint __APP_MODULE__Web.Endpoint
+
+  when_ "I visit the application home page", fn world ->
+    Map.put(world, :response, get(build_conn(), "/"))
+  end
+
+  then_ "the application renders its welcome page", fn world ->
+    assert html_response(world.response, 200) =~ "Peace of mind"
+    world
+  end
+end
+ACCEPTANCE
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/support/env.ex" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+# Acceptance tests must use test-only dependencies and configuration.
+unless Mix.env() == :test do
+  raise "Run acceptance tests in MIX_ENV=test"
+end
+ACCEPTANCE
+    ;;
+  mix)
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/greeting.feature" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+Feature: Library greetings
+  Scenario: Greet a named recipient
+    When I greet "Ada"
+    Then the greeting is "hello Ada"
+ACCEPTANCE
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/step_definitions/greeting_steps.ex" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+defmodule __APP_MODULE__.GreetingSteps do
+  use Cucumberex.DSL
+  import ExUnit.Assertions
+
+  when_ "I greet {string}", fn world, recipient ->
+    Map.put(world, :greeting, __APP_MODULE__.greet([recipient]))
+  end
+
+  then_ "the greeting is {string}", fn world, expected ->
+    assert world.greeting == expected
+    world
+  end
+end
+ACCEPTANCE
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/support/env.ex" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+# Acceptance tests must use test-only dependencies and configuration.
+unless Mix.env() == :test do
+  raise "Run acceptance tests in MIX_ENV=test"
+end
+ACCEPTANCE
+    ;;
+  escript)
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/greeting.feature" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+Feature: Command line greetings
+  Scenario: Greet a named recipient successfully
+    When I run the greeting command for "Ada"
+    Then the command succeeds with "hello Ada"
+
+  Scenario: Reject an unsupported output format
+    When I request the unsupported format "xml"
+    Then the command reports a usage error
+ACCEPTANCE
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/step_definitions/greeting_steps.ex" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+defmodule __APP_MODULE__.GreetingSteps do
+  use Cucumberex.DSL
+  import ExUnit.Assertions
+
+  when_ "I run the greeting command for {string}", fn world, recipient ->
+    Map.put(world, :result, __APP_MODULE__.CLI.run([recipient]))
+  end
+
+  then_ "the command succeeds with {string}", fn world, expected ->
+    assert world.result == {expected, 0}
+    world
+  end
+
+  when_ "I request the unsupported format {string}", fn world, format ->
+    Map.put(world, :result, __APP_MODULE__.CLI.run(["--format", format]))
+  end
+
+  then_ "the command reports a usage error", fn world ->
+    assert {message, 2} = world.result
+    assert message =~ "unknown format: xml"
+    assert message =~ "Usage:"
+    world
+  end
+end
+ACCEPTANCE
+    sed "s/__APP_MODULE__/$APP_MODULE/g" > "$APP_DIR/features/support/env.ex" <<'ACCEPTANCE'
+# Acceptance tests must use test-only dependencies and configuration.
+unless Mix.env() == :test do
+  raise "Run acceptance tests in MIX_ENV=test"
+end
+ACCEPTANCE
+    ;;
+esac

+# Manual documentation injection keeps its documented optional dependency policy.
+Dir.mktmpdir('acceptance-manual-injection') do |work|
+  {'default' => nil, 'custom' => '{:jason, "~> 1.4"}', 'empty' => ''}.each do |mode, selection|
+    app = File.join(work, mode, 'acceptance_app')
+    FileUtils.mkdir_p(app)
+    File.write(File.join(app, 'mix.exs'), <<~ELIXIR)
+      defmodule AcceptanceApp.MixProject do
+        use Mix.Project
+        def project, do: [app: :acceptance_app, deps: deps()]
+        defp deps do
+          [
+            {:phoenix, "~> 1.8"},
+          ]
+        end
+      end
+    ELIXIR
+    command = [{'APP_EXTRA_DEPS' => selection, 'CD_NO_SETUP' => '1'}, 'bash',
+               File.join(ROOT, 'scripts/inject-skill-docs.sh'), app]
+    run!(*command)
+    dependencies = read_utf8(File.join(app, 'mix.exs'))
+    if mode == 'default'
+      ['{:req, "~> 0.5"}', '{:oban, "~> 2.19"}',
+       '{:cucumberex, "~> 0.2.1", only: [:dev, :test]}',
+       '{:protox, "~> 2.0.8", only: [:dev, :test]}'].each do |dependency|
+        assert(dependencies.include?(dependency), "manual injection omitted #{dependency}")
+      end
+    else
+      assert(!dependencies.match?(/\{:(?:req|oban|cucumberex|protox),/), "manual #{mode} injection ignored APP_EXTRA_DEPS")
+      assert(dependencies.include?(selection), 'manual custom dependency missing') unless selection.empty?
+    end
+    run!(*command)
+    assert(dependencies == read_utf8(File.join(app, 'mix.exs')), 'manual injection duplicated dependencies on rerun')
+  end
+end
